sources.citation: Bosquet L, Berryman N, Dupuy O, Mekary S, Arvisais D, Bherer L, Mujika I. Effect of training cessation on muscular performance: a meta-analysis. Scand J Med Sci Sports 2013;23(3):e140-e149. doi:10.1111/sms.12047.
sources.usedFor: Strength detraining has a dose-response with the duration of cessation and is larger in inactive and older people; a few weeks without training is a material but bounded loss. Supports reading the H28 strength resumption as SUBOPTIMAL, not UNSAFE. Group means; not an individual prediction; muscle mass not studied.

sources.citation: Nosaka K, Sakamoto K, Newton M, Sacco P. How long does the protective effect on eccentric exercise-induced muscle damage last? Med Sci Sports Exerc 2001;33(9):1490-1495.
sources.usedFor: The repeated-bout protection after one bout persists for weeks to months for most markers (elbow flexors, maximal eccentric). Supports that a three-week strength lapse does not remove all protection, so the H28 dose risk is mainly soreness. Low applicability: upper-limb maximal eccentric model, not lower-body bodyweight work.

verdictBasis: Domain side of R7D-PREREG-1 §4, read with PREREG-2 to -8. (1) All registered coverage items are met by valid, evaluable cases; there is no CORPUS_ERROR. (2) No domain-judged property part fails: P07, P08 strength and identity, P09 step size and P12 interference pass; P14 influence with consent is not exercised. The 17 P06, P08 and P18 units the run left not evaluable each get a domain result of PASS, and the 11 P03 units a domain reading of PASS. They stay NOT_EVALUABLE in the automated tally. (3) There is no SAFETY, SCIENTIFIC or GENERALIZATION blocker from the domain side, and no UNSAFE step. (4) Rubric: 23 BEST_SUPPORTED, 14 ACCEPTABLE_ALTERNATIVE and 2 SUBOPTIMAL (H07, H28). Both SUBOPTIMAL cases are attributed to AUTHORITY_SCOPE: the runtime applies a bound reading as written, and each is a disclosed residual. So neither blocks (§4.4). (5) None of the 11 failed author expectations is a runtime failure: 9 are acceptable alternatives and 2 are EXPECTATION_OUTSIDE_AUTHORITY. (6) The two Phase 4 blockers hold on the new cases. The verdict is domain-only (r2 C3): the automated results, freeze, seal, harness and independence rulings belong to the Quality judge, and a Quality NOT_READY stands on its own.

conditions.text: Consumer conditions stay binding (SSCTR r2 C1, from Phase 4 CND-4). (a) C2: a REQUIRES_RECONCILIATION projection is never presented as a prescription. This holdout has athletes who trained for weeks under open questions: H08 s1-s3, H20, H32 s2-s5, H34. (b) C3 with R5: reports sent under an eligibility clinical flag are re-sent or re-asked after clearance. In H18 and H19 the weeks 0-1 reports sent with the flag never reached the record, so the moderate return had no executed pre-break reference (entry dose used; conservative). (c) The P12 same-turn confirmation (H04; 426 H2 observations). (d) The G03 wording of the reason-screen question and of the R4 HOLD. In H05 s4 the HOLD reason is an internal exception text; in H33 s4 'missing interruption.startedAt' is said of an event that carried it.

The Quality judge rules on everything this record does not: criterion 1 and 2 integrity, determinism, idempotence, the seal and freshness, the host-injected context disclosure of the author, HARNESS-9 versus HARNESS-8, K-P5-2 (P06 units dropped without listing, QRE-P5-F03) and the validity of the CARRIER_CLINICAL and CARRIER_HOLD units. A Quality finding that removes a unit counted below reopens the coverage clause it supports.

These are routed, not fixed here, and none is a new holdout failure: SSCTR-P5H-O01 (the free-text reason screen over-triggers), SSCTR-P5H-O02 (a race week with no strength planned re-enters strength), SSCTR-P5H-O03 (when the return week is empty, the conditional next week is the first prescription and can carry a step), SSCTR-P5H-O04 (an onboarding pause under four weeks is not read by the in-program return classes), and the carried SSCTR-P5-O02, -O05 and -O06 (r2 C2). Owners: the policy owner and PCG with the G04 owner (O01, O02, O04), G03 and Product-UX (O01 wording, O03 presentation), and the next functional mission.

SSCTR-P4-F01 is closed only on the shapes this holdout reaches: no exercise with a record before a moderate break (H18, H19), and exercises with valid history (H02, H15, H21, H23, H35, H36). The exact Phase 4 mixed shape does not occur in H1: some exercises with executed history and others planned and never executed before the break. It rests on T42-T44 and the Phase 5 review witnesses, and QRE-P5-F01 (TEST_GAP, mutant J3) stays carried under K-P5-1.
This record grants no V1 coaching authority, no human, empirical or clinical validation, and no G01-G04 closure. F08 stays F08_OPEN, and the D2 direction is not implemented.

findings.evidence: screenInterruptionReason, run in memory on every corpus break text. H07: 'caring for my mother after her operation' gives CLINICAL (matched 'operation'), so s1 and s2 are CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED and the route is sticky. H20: 'long weekend in the mountains, back on Wednesday' gives ASK (matched 'back'). H32: 'trade show, on my feet all week' gives ASK ('feet'). H34: 'a new baby in the family' gives ASK ('baby'). In all four the category is nonclinical and nonclinical is true. Every other break text in H1 screens NONCLINICAL.
findings.domainReading: Fail-closed: no dose is planned. H34 is the most defensible ask, because 'new baby' can mean postpartum, a clinical category in the interface's own list. H20 and H32 are idiomatic uses of a body word, and H07 is a third-party mention. Each costs one question with an exit (re-send the break with a clear reason), except H07. There R-F08-1 keeps the athlete with a human at every later decision until a G04 owner exists. That is the disclosed free-text false-positive lock (PREREG-6 Δ9, R-F08-1 R1/R2), and the PCG authority states that a clinical mention in free text routes and is sticky. Within V1 authority no disambiguation rule exists, so the attribution is AUTHORITY_SCOPE.
findings.routing: PCG with the G04 owner: the lexicon for third-party and idiomatic mentions, and the stickiness of a free-text-only clinical match. G03 and Product-UX: collect the structured category and keep free text optional, or ask a disambiguation question. Next functional mission. No rule proposed here.

findings.origin: PRE_EXISTING (BR-Q1.2(b) with BR-Q4.4 since Phase 3.4; the same reading as QRE-P34-05, ruled a disclosed residual by SSCTR r2)
findings.evidence: H28's week 8 is a race week. Its strength days are REST_BY_DESIGN, so no strength session is planned. The touch and the race were done, and the optional shakeout's adverse recovery is a single signal that does not converge. The holiday (2026-12-30 to 2027-01-05) is therefore read TRAINING_AFTER, re-entry week 2027-01-06, and the latest stop is SHORT (4 days). Last executed strength: 2026-12-28. Next strength: 2027-01-20, at goblet-squat 3x10@3 22 kg, incline-push-up 3x12@3 and db-row 3x10@3 18 kg. The exposure is phasedSets 3 = baseSets 3 in NEXT_BLOCK. In week 6 the same rows were 2 sets (SPECIFIC phase reduction from base 3). That is about 22 days without strength. A 22-day stop inside the program would be MODERATE (moderateMaxDays 28): entry at 1 set, RIR at least 4.
findings.domainReading: The runtime applies the bound reading literally. A week re-enters fully when every sport it plans re-enters (BR-Q4.4), and a sport with no live session in that week is not planned in it (the QRE-P34-05 ruling). It credits no progression: the 3 sets are the base count earned before the race block, restored when the phase reduction ends. The consequence is still a strength restart one step above the last executed sets after three weeks without strength, for a novice lifter. That is worse than the return recipe the authority applies when a strength lapse is classed (SUBOPTIMAL). It is not unsafe: bodyweight and light dumbbells at RIR 3. S4: detraining is dose-dependent but bounded over a few weeks. S5: repeated-bout protection persists for weeks. The race-week form makes the reading reachable in ordinary use, which the QRE-P34-05 text (sessions marked unavailable) did not name. Evidence status for the harm: PLAUSIBLE_BUT_UNCERTAIN (soreness more than injury).
findings.routing: Policy owner (BR-Q4.4 author line) and the next functional mission: whether a sport with no live session in the re-entry week should read its own lapse. No dose or number proposed.

findings.evidence: In both cases the return report comes late in its week, and every session left in that week is past or rest. The conditional next week (b+1) is then the first prescription after the return. In H27 week 9 (NEXT_BLOCK), goblet-squat, push-up and db-row are 3x10@3 or 3x12@3 (base 3 restored). The executed doses were 2 sets in SPECIFIC and 1x10@4 in the race week. H28 is the same pattern (SSCTR-P5H-O02).
findings.domainReading: Inside the registered envelope: next week conditional, at most one step above the review, never in the week of the answer and never a race touch. The SHORT recipe's 'no step until execution is observed' is honoured in the letter, because the return week holds the resumption. In practice the first executed week after the return carries the step. Magnitude: one set at RIR 3. Consumer condition C9: present the following weeks as provisional.
findings.routing: G03 / Product-UX (presentation of b+1 as provisional) and the next functional mission.

findings.origin: PRE_EXISTING (R6 intake rule QRE-R6-12: a pause of four weeks or more restarts)
findings.evidence: Two generated intakes declare a nonclinical pause under four weeks. G068 (2 weeks): week 0 has EASY 40 x3 and LONG 50 (recent longest 54). G123 (3 weeks): LONG 55 (recent longest 57) and the known strength doses, kb-goblet-squat 4x10@3 15 kg plus glute-bridge 4x12@3 and reverse-lunge 4x12@3 on two consecutive lower days. Every intake whose pause is four weeks or more restarts (15-20 min easy or walk/jog; strength at effort-guided establishment, at most 2 sets, RIR 3).
findings.domainReading: D18 bounds both run doses, and RIR self-regulates the strength. The same 14- or 21-day stop inside the program would be read MODERATE (entry 15/20 min, 1 set RIR at least 4), so the onboarding and in-program readings of an equal stop differ. The onboarding path is less conservative between 11 and 27 days. This is not R7-D runtime work.
findings.routing: Policy owner and the next functional mission (the coherence of the intake pause rule with operational.return).

findings.evidence: A DOUBLE_CONFLICT for one date (2026-11-30, both sessions PM, same turn confirmed) gives ASK: 'a dated window of days or shifts is not re-planned automatically; say whether the change is permanent from a date, or move or skip the affected sessions'.
findings.domainReading: No dose changes, and the day concerned is an upper-body strength day with an easy run, so no interference question arises. The ask is safe and keeps agency, at the cost of one question.

findings.evidence: loadsByPattern values the author meant for barbell lifts reach dumbbell rows. founderDomainQuestions.question: Coherence of the running progression
founderDomainQuestions.answer: Coherent. Long runs rise about 5 min a week and hold after adverse, contradictory or future-clocked facts. Tapers cut volume, keep intensity and add a race touch, and post-event weeks are recovery only. Walk/jog ladders progress by interval. Late reporters advance one step behind. D18 bounds every dose: 0 P06 violations, and every not-evaluable unit passes on domain review.

founderDomainQuestions.question: Coherence of the strength progression
founderDomainQuestions.answer: Coherent where loads are known. Reps progress before sets at RIR3. Barbell loads rise 2.5 kg. Machines progress by 'next setting above', with one question per setting and an equal second log adopting it; a missed heavier attempt is asked, not adopted. First logged loads are confirmed before they become numbers, and RIR-less logs never count. Band rows progress. Limitation: dumbbell load magnitudes logged by pattern are not evaluable (O06).

founderDomainQuestions.question: Interference between the two
founderDomainQuestions.answer: Handled within the chosen days. Lower-body strength goes with easy running and split turns, and strength stays off the day before the long run where possible. Race-week strength is light, early or rested. Same-day quality with strength happens only on an athlete-chosen shared day, hours apart. No change was needed for interference alone (overlap is not interference).

founderDomainQuestions.question: Response to fatigue and recovery
founderDomainQuestions.answer: Proportionate. Local fatigue removes optional local work. Systemic convergence across sports blocks re-entry. A confounded run with adverse recovery stays adverse and holds the long run. A single hard run holds and does not lower. Systemic fatigue after a return keeps a plan with no quality and no step. A repeated local signal gets the same minimal change before a consolidation week (H37; acceptable, not more).

founderDomainQuestions.question: Preservation of demonstrated capacity
founderDomainQuestions.answer: Preserved. Known loads come back after the return steps (H21, H23, H36), and executed history is never erased (H08, H27, H29-H31). A full low-load week between breaks resumes the pre-break doses (O-01, H09). A short demonstration informs the restart without restoring the old doses (H36).

founderDomainQuestions.question: Safety of the return after breaks
founderDomainQuestions.answer: Safe on every valid case. The class table applies: SHORT up to 10 days resumes the last doses; MODERATE (11-28 days) enters at 15/20 min and 1 set RIR4 or more, then 2 conditional steps; LONG restarts. Separate breaks are read by re-entry, own return or continuity, and never summed or dropped. Clinical comes first, and the F08 lock holds. Residuals, none unsafe: strength after a race week that plans none (H28, O02), b+1 carrying a step when the return week is empty (H27, H28, O03), the F04 strength-lapse reading (H29), onboarding pauses under 4 weeks (H2 G068, G123, O04), and over-triggered reason screening (O01).

founderDomainQuestions.question: No progression without evidence
founderDomainQuestions.answer: Held. Unreported weeks are unknown, and questions are asked whenever a dose depends on them, CONSOLIDATION included (H16). Steps follow executed weeks only: 0 P09 violations, and H31 and H33 step after executed week 6. Late sessions do not raise doses. Partial or RIR-less logs do not advance (H08 exercise level, H30). EARNED needs repeated easier executions (H39). The base sets restored after a race block (H27, H28) are earned counts, not credit.

founderDomainQuestions.question: Compatibility with the existing sports authorities
founderDomainQuestions.answer: Compatible. The R6 policy is consistent: the return table, D18, taper and race-week strength rules, and the fatigue handler. The B0 catalog holds: 0 P11 violations, and equipment-only selections (kettlebell H09, bodyweight H06, travel substitutes H17). F03B-MACHINE-STEP-r1 is consistent (H03, H16). The BR-Q readings are applied as written, with the BR-Q4.4 edge routed (O02). CFD-1 to CFD-5 are read as disclosed.
